tagline.text: The Galapagos of Asia, alive with primeval forest and crystal-clear rivers

items.credit: Carlo Joseph Moskito / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: Never connected to any other landmass, this isolated island teems with endemic species and is known as the "Galapagos of Asia." From the jagged, 2,058-meter Mount Guiting-Guiting to the Cantingas River, said to be the cleanest in the Philippines, to forest waterfalls and white sandbars, you can encounter nature untouched by human hands.

Sibuyan Island is a round island of about 445 km² in the middle of the Sibuyan Sea, east of Romblon province. Three towns — Magdiwang, San Fernando, and Cajidiocan — line the coast, and Mount Guiting-Guiting, rising to 2,058 meters, stands at the island's center. Because the mountain climbs more than 2,000 meters directly from the coastline, from the sea the whole island looks like a single giant mountain.

Geologically, Sibuyan is known never to have been connected to any other landmass in the Philippines. Isolated for a very long time, it developed many plants and animals that evolved independently, leading scientists to call it the "Galapagos of Asia." Its primeval forest, stretching from lowland tropical forest through mossy forest to montane grassland, has recorded more than 700 species of vascular plants and about 130 species of birds, and one 1-hectare survey plot found 123 tree species. Nepenthes sibuyanensis, a pitcher plant found nowhere else on Earth, is also well known here.

The mountain has been protected as Mount Guiting-Guiting Natural Park since 1996, and water flowing down from its forests forms rivers and waterfalls across the island. The Cantingas River, in Taclobo village, San Fernando, has repeatedly won national awards as the cleanest inland body of water, and you can swim in its crystal-clear pools. Recently, opposition from residents and environmental groups over proposed nickel mining has kept the island's conservation in the national spotlight.

There are almost no resorts or amenities, and the journey there is long. Instead, you can stay in simple homestays prone to power outages, swim in the river, walk forest trails, and spend a slow day on the sandbar island of Cresta de Gallo. It's recommended for ecotourists seeking real nature and climbers looking to take on one of the Philippines' toughest mountains.

A clear river in Taclobo village, San Fernando, where you can swim in green pools so clear you can see the bottom, and jump in from the rocks. Mount Guiting-Guiting's peak forms the backdrop.
A small uninhabited island off San Fernando, ringed with white sand and coral reefs. Good for snorkeling in calm water and picnicking on the sandy beach.
A forest waterfall close to Magdiwang town, with a wide pool that's easy to stop by and swim in. The cold, clear water makes it a favorite picnic spot for locals.

children.text: If a summit climb feels too demanding, you can walk the lowland forest trails from the park entrance on the Magdiwang side for a few hours with a guide, observing giant trees, birds, and pitcher plants.

If attempting the summit climb, use Days 3 and 4 for the ascent, and add a rest day after descending, planning for a total of at least 5 nights and 6 days.

The main route from Manila is to take a Starlite Ferries roll-on/roll-off boat from Batangas port, via Romblon Island, to Ambulong port in Magdiwang, Sibuyan. It departs in the afternoon and arrives in the dead of night or at dawn, taking about
12 hours
, with fares of about
depending on seat class. Sailing days and times change often, so be sure to check the schedule first on the
Starlite Ferries official website

1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours

1 hour

1 PM

5 hours

30 minutes–1 hour
between towns. To visit several sights, a full-day chartered tricycle (about

February–May
brings the least rain and the calmest seas, making it the best time for boat travel, river and waterfall outings, and climbing Mount Guiting-Guiting. Coastal midday temperatures reach
, but up on the mountain, nights drop to around
, with fog and rain rolling in frequently. Mount Guiting-Guiting closes to climbers for part of
November–January
for maintenance and forest recovery, so check the park office's latest notices.
June–December

is the wet season and typhoon period, when swollen rivers make swimming dangerous and boats crossing the Sibuyan Sea are often cancelled. The seas are dangerous during typhoon season — in 2008 a passenger ferry capsized off this island's coast with heavy loss of life — so postpone boat travel whenever a weather warning is issued.

Lodging is mostly homestays, guesthouses, and small beach resorts in Magdiwang and San Fernando towns, running about

a night. Magdiwang, home to the park office, is convenient if you're focused on climbing Mount Guiting-Guiting or visiting Lambingan Falls, while San Fernando is handier for the Cantingas River and Cresta de Gallo. Many places can't be booked online, so reserving through a Facebook page or by phone is common, and power and internet outages are frequent, so it's best to stay with a relaxed mindset.
Food here is a simple country table. At town carinderias, a meal of stewed fish, sautéed vegetables, or a coconut milk dish with rice costs about

. With clear rivers and the sea nearby, freshwater shrimp, fish, and crab are fresh, and you can also try tuba, a traditional wine fermented from coconut sap. Restaurants close early and options are limited, so prepare a packed lunch and snacks the day before a climb or island-hopping trip.
The island has almost no ATMs, and card payment is difficult too. Withdraw enough cash for your whole stay in Batangas or on Romblon Island.

Climbing Mount Guiting-Guiting requires registering at the park office (DENR and the park management board) in Magdiwang, attending an orientation, and climbing with an assigned guide. Climber quotas and fees can change, so contact them in advance to confirm.
Under the

Protected Area Management Board (PAMB) rules, climbing to the summit requires certificates for at least two recent major climbs, with an exemption if you only go as far as Camp 1, Camp 2, or Mayo's Peak. A medical certificate and ID are required for everyone, and the detailed criteria change often, so check with the park office first.
The climb requires gloves, a helmet, and a light waterproof jacket. The rock ridges are sharp and become slippery in the rain.
Avoid using sunscreen and shampoo in the rivers and waterfalls. Keeping the water clean is a matter of courtesy when visiting this island.
Cell signal is often available only in town centers. Write down your accommodation and boat contact numbers in advance.
Boat schedules are irregular, so confirm your return sailing as soon as you arrive, and leave at least one spare day before any flight or departure date.
Mosquitoes and biting flies are common, so wear long clothing and use insect repellent in the forest and along riverbanks.
Boats to Cresta de Gallo are rented at Azagra port in San Fernando, taking about
1–2 hours
each way depending on waves. A day trip runs about
for 1–4 people and about

Mount Guiting-Guiting is one of the Philippines' hardest and most dangerous mountains, with a history of falls and climbers going missing. If you don't have enough climbing experience, opt for the lowland forest trek instead, and be sure to check the park office's latest regulations and weather information before any climb.
Rivers can rise suddenly after rain, so don't swim in the Cantingas River or waterfalls, and stay away from the water's edge after rainfall.
Before jumping into the river from the rocks, check the water depth first, and don't jump where there's no local guidance.
Collecting plants or insects, and taking pitcher plants out of the protected area, are prohibited.
Protests or rallies over the mining issue sometimes take place; keep your distance and check local news.
The island has no major hospital, so transferring an injured person takes a long time. Bring travel insurance and a first-aid kit.

An island at the southern tip of Romblon province, known for white sand beaches and cliff diving. Getting there requires passing through Romblon Island and Tablas, taking more than a day.
The Philippines' foremost beach resort, reached via Roxas City and about 3 hours overland along Panay Island — a lively contrast to quiet Sibuyan.
A heart-shaped island north across the Sibuyan Sea, known for the Holy Week Moriones Festival and its fortress church. Check in advance for boat connections via Romblon Island.
